Your literature search

Use m, k, b, or derive k and b from m, fn, ζ.

k = m(2πfn)²
b = 2ζm(2πfn)

Check that fn is the undamped natural frequency and that all parameters describe the same mode.

Optional: use COMSOL to extract structural parameters for the same mode and coordinate.

MODEL

The coordinate fixes the input sign

x = y − z    a = d²y/dt²

m ẍ + b ẋ + kx = ma(t)
X(s)A(s)=1s² + (b/m)s + k/m

Input: casing acceleration a(t).
Output: relative displacement x(t).

Zero initial conditions: x(0) = 0 and ẋ(0) = 0.

Derivation and the opposite sign convention

The mass obeys m z̈ = b(ẏ − ż) + k(y − z). With x = y − z, z̈ = a − ẍ, which gives m ẍ + b ẋ + kx = ma. Choosing x = z − y gives a negative input term instead.

These values are assumed for teaching. They do not describe a measured device.

PREDICT BEFORE RUNNING

0.2484 μm/g

Static displacement sensitivity

xstatic / a = m/k = 1/ωn²

1g = 9.80665 m/s². A 2g input predicts 0.4968 μm of displacement in this linear model.

Model Workspace definitions
m = 1e-6;
fn_hz = 1000;
zeta = 0.7;
wn = 2*pi*fn_hz;
k = m*wn^2;
b = 2*zeta*m*wn;
g0 = 9.80665;
input_g = 1;
step_time = 0.005;
freq_hz = 100;
input_mode = 0;

Open Model Explorer (daexplr), select this model's Model Workspace, choose MATLAB Code, paste the definitions, then select Reinitialize from Source and save.

BUILD

The first model is a four-block chain

The transfer-function output is in meters. Convert to μm only for display.

Starting from a blank model

In MATLAB, run simulink. Choose Blank Model, save the file, then double-click the canvas and type each block name. Use the Simulink library's Step, Transfer Fcn, Gain and Scope blocks.

BUILD

The equation becomes two integrators and feedback

ẍ = a − (b/m)ẋ − (k/m)x

Keep the feedback Gains positive. The negative signs belong in the Sum block.

BUILD

One input drives both mechanical realizations

Instructor-supplied model screenshot

Input selection
0 selects Step, 1 selects Sine.

Shared Scope
Two 1e6 Gains and a two-input Mux.

SI data logs
a_mps2, x_tf_m and x_ode_m.

Switch and logging settings

Switch: top port = Sine, middle port = Constant input_mode, bottom port = Step. Set criterion to u2 >= Threshold and threshold to 0.5. Connect its output to both mechanical branches.

Use three To Workspace blocks with Timeseries format. Log displacement before the 1e6 Gains. Enable Single simulation output to access out.a_mps2, out.x_tf_m and out.x_ode_m.

RUN

A continuous model needs a suitable integration step

Model Settings Ctrl + E

Solver typeFixed-step
Solverode4 (Runge–Kutta)
Fixed-step size1e-6 s
Stop time0.03 s for Step

The first run

  1. Set input_mode = 0.
  2. Run, open Scope, and use Autoscale.
  3. Check a 1g step at t = 5 ms.
  4. Confirm both outputs overlap.

Source Sample time = 0 means continuous input. It is different from the solver's 1 μs integration step.

Sine input settings and common mistakes

Sine Wave: time-based, amplitude input_g*g0, frequency 2*pi*freq_hz in rad/s, zero bias and phase, Sample time 0. Use 80 ms at 100 Hz, and 30 ms at 1000 or 5000 Hz.

If a parameter edit has no effect, check the Model Workspace. If the response grows unexpectedly, check Sum signs +-- and the two feedback Gains.

RESULTS · SAVED SIMULINK OUTPUT

Both models predict the same step response

Transfer FcnTwo integrators
Final displacement0.2484 μm
Overshoot4.60 %
2% settling time0.952 ms

Settling time starts at the input step. The maximum difference between the models is 1.29e-26 m.

Metric definitions and theoretical checks

The static displacement is g0*m/k. Overshoot is (max(x)/x_final - 1)*100%. The measured settling time is the final exit from the steady-state value ±2% band. The common approximation 4/(zeta*wn) gives 0.909 ms, which is an estimate rather than an exact prediction.

RESULTS

Damping changes the transient and resonance

Same m and k

Static sensitivity remains m/k. Only the damping coefficient changes.

Your literature-based experiment

  1. Cite the parameter source and state the assumptions.
  2. Build both equivalent mechanical models.
  3. Measure step-response metrics and compare with theory.
  4. Explain damping, gain and phase using the plots.

This linear mechanical model predicts displacement. Electrical sensitivity, noise and structural nonlinearity require additional models.

AI-assisted work: add a short “AI use and verification” subsection. Record each agent/tool name, version when visible, model provider and exact displayed model/version, and the parts of the work it supported.

SKILL PROJECT · AI ROUTE

One small function is enough

Turn your technical knowledge into instructions that another agent can follow and you can verify.

What the skill contains

  1. Purpose and inputs

    When to use it, what information it needs, and what it produces.

  2. Technical basis and workflow

    Cited sources, assumptions and specific execution steps.

  3. Checks and limits

    How to judge the output and handle missing or unsuitable inputs.

  4. Reusable package

    A SKILL.md file, with scripts, references or templates as needed. Code is optional.

Example functions

Build a Simulink modelUse m, b, k to create and run one mechanical branch.
Extract literature parametersRecord values, units, source locations and missing data.
Convert parametersConvert m, fn, ζ to k, b and check consistency.
Analyze response dataCalculate sensitivity, overshoot or settling time.
Generate Bode plotsProduce magnitude and phase with stated conventions.
Estimate capacitive readoutConvert displacement to capacitance for a specified ideal geometry.

AI may help write the skill. Explain your own choices, improvements and verification.

Scope, reuse and documentation

Choose a narrow function. Full device design, complete COMSOL automation and compatibility with every agent are not required. State the agent, model and software environment you tested.

You may improve an existing open-source skill. Cite its source and identify your changes. A collection of papers or a generic prompt needs an actionable workflow and output checks to qualify.

Include brief usage instructions and an example input/output. Keep dependencies and input units explicit. See the Agent Skills format specification for the package structure.

Report checklist, sharing and COMSOL rubric

Skill report: purpose and technical sources; implementation and dependencies; agent/tool and exact displayed LLM model; your contribution; three test records and limitations; repository URL and tested commit or release.

Sharing: a public GitHub repository with a README and license is encouraged. A teacher-accessible private repository or download link is also acceptable. Reference papers by citation or link unless you have permission to redistribute them.

Document the tested environment, sample inputs, expected outputs and acceptance criteria. Numerical tolerances should match the task. Tests must show actual runs. Complete chat histories and an oral demonstration are not required.

COMSOL bonus, also up to 10 points: correct model and physical assumptions (3); mesh refinement and independent validation (3); consistent parameter extraction and Simulink connection (2); clear report and reproducible model (2). This rubric applies only to assessed work completed without AI.
